newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah steady in slow late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah steady in slow late trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was steady against the dollar in late trading on Monday, dealers said.

They said trading was slow due to a public holiday in the United States. One local bank dealer said the dollar came under some pressure after the central bank kept its intervention rate unchanged at 2,320/2,512 late on Monday.
The conversion rate was kept at 2,320/2,368.
"Some players may want to test the downside of the central bank band again. But I don't think it would have any impact as trading was lacklustre," the local bank dealer said.

Economists said earlier the central bank would have no problem in supporting the dollar if it does touch the floor rate because it could neutralise additional monetary supply through short-term securities (SBIs).
They said outstanding SBIs were much lower now compared to last year and M2 money supply aggregates were declining.
Year-on-year M2 growth in August was 26.32 percent against 28.74 percent in July. M2 growth in June was 29.83 percent and in May it was at 30.8 percent.
Dealers said players were seen selling dollars immediately after the fixing was announced.
They said it was not clear whether the central bank had bought dollars in the market or not as some buyers had quoted the dollar slightly below the floor rate.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,319.5/20.5 at 0900 GMT against an opening of 2,321.25/22.00. Tomorrow was at 2,319.1/19.3.
One Japanese bank dealer said sentiment on the rupiah remained firm and the focus was on liquidity and the band.
"Tuesday liquidity is the issue now. But I don't think it will be extremely tight tomorrow," the local bank dealer said.
He said an easing in overnight money to 11.0 percent in the afternoon may indicate possible relaxed conditions on Tuesday.
Weekly tax payments and bank liquidity reports are due on Tuesday. Overnight money opened at 18.0 percent on Monday.
"You don't have alternative financing through overnight swaps today and the market is still well supplied. I think Tuesday liquidity would be okay," the dealer said.
However, short-dated swap rates remained expensive, with tom/next swap quoted at 0.85/0.90 points.
But longer-term swaps were easier, dealers said.
One-month swap edged down to 20.25/21.25 from 21.0/22.0, two to 36.25/37.50 from 37.25/38.75, three to 53.50/54.50 from 55.0/56.5 and six to 103.50/105.00 from 105.0/107.0 points.
